item.text:
**3B.1 Research Note: Abiy Ahmed in 2024**

**Bottom line:** The 2024 evidence is strongly negative. I found widespread reports of arbitrary detention, enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings, and attacks on civilians and medical care by Ethiopian security forces, with no credible public evidence that Abiy accepted responsibility or meaningfully restrained the abuses. The only modest positive evidence is limited oversight / monitoring and IHL training.

| Date | Title | Publisher | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-03-04 | Ethiopia’s Deepening Crackdown on Dissent | Human Rights Watch | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/04/ethiopias-deepening-crackdown-dissent | HRW said Ethiopia’s authorities detained opposition figures and journalists, used emergency powers, and made “no one” appear safe from arbitrary arrest and detention. This is strong evidence of political imprisonment and arbitrary detention. | 3B.1, 7A.* |
| 2024-06-18 | Ethiopia: Halt Crackdown Against Human Rights Groups | Human Rights Watch | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/ethiopia-halt-crackdown-against-human-rights-groups | HRW said security and intelligence forces followed, intimidated, and threatened human-rights workers since February 2024, including at homes and offices. This is strong evidence of state intimidation and suppression of civic actors. | 3B.1, 7A.* |
| 2024-10-01 | Ethiopia: Mass arbitrary detentions in Amhara region deepen erosion of rule of law | Amnesty International | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/10/ethiopia-mass-arbitrary-detentions-in-amhara-region-deepen-erosion-of-rule-of-law/ | Amnesty reported ongoing arbitrary mass detentions of hundreds of people in Amhara, often without warrants and without timely court appearance. This is direct evidence of arbitrary punishment and unlawful detention. | 3B.1, 7A.* |
| 2024-07-03 | Ethiopia: Army Attacks Health Care in Amhara Conflict | Human Rights Watch | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/03/ethiopia-army-attacks-health-care-amhara-conflict | HRW documented soldiers beating, arresting, and intimidating medical staff, seizing ambulances, and attacking medical transports and hospitals. This is strong evidence of unlawful violence and disregard for protected persons. | 3B.1, 7A.* |
| 2024-04-04 | Ethiopia: Military Executes Dozens in Amhara Region | Human Rights Watch | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/04/ethiopia-military-executes-dozens-amhara-region | HRW said Ethiopian military forces summarily killed dozens of civilians in Merawi and committed other war crimes. This is direct evidence of extrajudicial killing and failure to protect residents from state violence. | 3B.1, 7A.* |
| 2024-01-12 | Country policy and information note: actors of protection, Ethiopia, February 2024 (accessible) | GOV.UK | https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ethiopia-country-policy-and-information-notes/country-policy-and-information-note-actors-of-protection-ethiopia-february-2024-accessible | The note says the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission receives complaints and that some recommendations on human-rights protections and prison conditions were implemented. This is weak positive evidence of limited accountability infrastructure, but not proof of protection from abuse. | 3B.1 |
| 2024-09-13 | ICRC Impact in Ethiopia: January - June 2024 Bulletin | International Committee of the Red Cross | https://www.icrc.org/en/article/ethiopia-bulletin-january-june-2024 | The ICRC said it maintained dialogue and training on IHL/IHRL for Ethiopian armed actors, aiming to improve respect for civilians and medical personnel. This is a limited positive signal, but it is training, not demonstrated protection or accountability. | 3B.1, 2B.4, 1B.7 |
| 2024-02-15 | Ethiopia troops denied massacre in Merawi as West calls for probe | Associated Press | https://apnews.com/article/ethiopia-troops-violence-fano-amhara-ba26d3c99bd03378ead8b65732814c96 | Ethiopian officials denied allegations that troops massacred civilians in Merawi while rights bodies and Western governments called for an investigation. This is evidence of denial in response to serious allegations, not acceptance of responsibility. | 3B.1, 2B.9 |

**Search gap**

- I searched directly for 2024 evidence of protection from torture, disappearances, political imprisonment, extrajudicial killing, and arbitrary punishment.
- I found no reliable public evidence that Abiy accepted responsibility for the abuses or implemented meaningful corrective accountability in 2024.
- I also found no strong evidence of a genuine reform turnaround on detention or security-force discipline in the same year.
- The small positive evidence is limited to complaint mechanisms, prison-condition recommendations, and IHL/IHRL training.

**Assessment**

- Best positive evidence: weak oversight / complaint channels and ICRC training.
- Best negative evidence: arbitrary detentions, enforced disappearance allegations, civilian executions, attacks on medical care, and repression of human-rights workers.
- Overall: 2024 looks like a clear failure to protect residents from state violence and arbitrary punishment.
